children: Abu Dhabi’s Space42 an AI-powered spacetech company, and US satellite communications firm Viasat will commit up to $1 billion in initial equity to set up Equatys, a shared space and ground infrastructure platform aimed at expanding mobile connectivity beyond the reach of terrestrial networks.

The agreement to formally establish the venture was signed at World Space Business Week in Paris. The companies also signed a separate agreement to increase joint funding and accelerate development of Equatys' initial satellite constellation.

Space42 and Viasat will each make an initial equity contribution of $400 million to Equatys, with the Abu Dhabi ADX-listed company expected to invest a further $200 million through a future equity funding round that will be open to third-party investors, bringing the founders' combined commitment to as much as $1 billion.
Funding for the company is expected to come from a combination of founders' equity, third-party equity and debt financing.
Equatys will support extended mobile coverage and network overlay services in underserved regions and terrestrial coverage gaps, including in densely populated urban areas.

The venture comes as demand for satellite-enabled mobile connectivity grows, driven by 3GPP Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) standards that allow smartphones and connected devices to connect directly to satellite networks.
The establishment of the venture, procurement of the satellite constellation and execution of related definitive agreements remain subject to customary closing conditions.

Space42, whose shareholders include G42 Holding Ltd., sovereign investor Mubadala, and International Holding Company, was formed by merging Yahsat Space Services (YSS) and Bayanat Smart Solutions (BSS).
(Writing by Brinda Darasha; editing by Seban Scaria)

title: Abu Dhabi’s Space42, Viasat to invest up to $1bln in satellite connectivity venture
